meta.title: Psique — Know yourself for real
meta.description: Personality tests, a multidimensional political spectrum, the dark triad and more. Every test fills your profile; your profile gives you insights and correlations.
meta.disclaimer: Psique is a self-knowledge and entertainment tool. No result is a clinical diagnosis or professional advice.

home.eyebrow: The test that won't flatter you
home.title: Know yourself
home.subtitle: Your political spectrum across 6 dimensions. Your personality, scientifically. Your inner villain. Your pushover level. Every test fills your profile — and your profile tells you what's coming: the good, the bad and the weird.
home.how1Body: Short, direct, no trick questions. Each one measures specific traits from a shared space of {traits} dimensions.
home.how2Body: Political compass in 2D and 3D, personality radar, villain level… Your profile grows with every test.
home.how3Body: Strengths, risks and oddities of your particular mix of traits, and how you compare to the rest of the community.

econ.name: Economic axis
econ.description: How much you favour redistribution and public intervention (0) versus free markets and low intervention (100).

auth.name: Authority axis
auth.description: How much you value individual freedom (0) versus order and state authority (100).

cult.name: Cultural axis
cult.description: Your stance on social change: embrace it (0) or protect established ways of life (100).

glob.name: Territorial axis
glob.description: International cooperation and global identity (0) versus sovereignty and national interest (100).

eco.name: Ecological axis
eco.description: Environment first even at an economic cost (0) versus growth first (100).

rel.name: Religious axis
rel.description: Strict separation of religion and public life (0) versus a public role for faith (100).

openness.name: Openness
openness.description: Intellectual curiosity, imagination and taste for the new versus a preference for the familiar.

conscientiousness.name: Conscientiousness
conscientiousness.description: Self-discipline, order and goal orientation versus improvisation.

extraversion.name: Extraversion
extraversion.description: How much energy you gain (or lose) from social contact.

agreeableness.name: Agreeableness
agreeableness.description: Empathy, trust in others and a tendency to cooperate rather than compete.

neuroticism.name: Neuroticism
neuroticism.description: How intensely you experience negative emotions: worry, mood swings, stress.

mach.name: Machiavellianism
mach.description: A tendency towards strategic manipulation and instrumental cynicism.

narc.name: Narcissism
narc.description: Need for admiration and a sense of being special.

psyc.name: Psychopathy
psyc.description: Emotional coldness, impulsivity and low guilt. (A trait, not a diagnosis.)

asert.name: Assertiveness
asert.description: Your ability to stand your ground and say what you think even when it's awkward.

complac.name: People pleasing
complac.description: How much you need others' approval and avoid letting people down.

confl.name: Conflict avoidance
confl.description: A tendency to dodge arguments even when the topic matters to you.

honesty.name: Honesty-Humility
honesty.description: The sixth HEXACO factor: sincerity, not exploiting others, and not feeling entitled to more.

care.name: Care
care.description: Sensitivity to the suffering of others: morality built on not doing harm.

fairness.name: Fairness
fairness.description: Reciprocity, rights and fair treatment as a moral basis.

loyalty.name: Loyalty
loyalty.description: Faithfulness to your own group: family, team, country.

authority.name: Authority
authority.description: Respect for hierarchy, tradition and legitimate order.

purity.name: Purity
purity.description: Notions of the sacred, of decency and of moral contamination.

liberty.name: Liberty
liberty.description: A gut rejection of domination and of being told how to live.

selfdir.name: Self-direction
selfdir.description: Thinking and acting on your own: independence and freedom of judgement.

stimul.name: Stimulation
stimul.description: A need for novelty, excitement and challenge.

hedon.name: Hedonism
hedon.description: Pleasure and sensory enjoyment as a value in itself.

achieve.name: Achievement
achieve.description: Personal success through demonstrating competence by social standards.

power.name: Power
power.description: Status, prestige and control over people and resources.

security.name: Security
security.description: Stability and harmony, both personal and societal.

conform.name: Conformity
conform.description: Restraining yourself so as not to upset or violate social expectations.

tradition.name: Tradition
tradition.description: Respect for and commitment to inherited customs.

benev.name: Benevolence
benev.description: Caring for the wellbeing of those close to you.

univers.name: Universalism
univers.description: Understanding and protecting the welfare of all people and of nature.

attachAnx.name: Attachment anxiety
attachAnx.description: Fear of abandonment and a need for reassurance in close relationships.

attachAvo.name: Intimacy avoidance
attachAvo.description: Discomfort with dependence and emotional closeness.

selfEmo.name: Emotional self-awareness
selfEmo.description: Knowing what you feel and why while you feel it, not three days later.

otherEmo.name: Reading others
otherEmo.description: Reading other people's emotional state from gestures, tones and silences.

useEmo.name: Using emotions
useEmo.description: Putting emotions to work: motivating yourself, prioritising, turning nerves into focus.

regEmo.name: Emotion regulation
regEmo.description: Turning an emotion's volume down when it isn't helping, without denying it.

humorAfil.name: Affiliative humour
humorAfil.description: Humour that bonds: jokes that include people and build the group.

humorSelf.name: Self-enhancing humour
humorSelf.description: Humour as your own shock absorber: laughing at the mess so it does not sink you.

humorAgr.name: Aggressive humour
humorAgr.description: Humour at other people’s expense: sarcasm, digs and targeted mockery.

humorDest.name: Self-defeating humour
humorDest.description: Humour at your own expense: putting yourself down to be liked or fit in.

selfesteem.name: Self-esteem
selfesteem.description: Your overall evaluation of yourself: how much you respect and like who you are.

locus.name: Locus of control
locus.description: What you attribute your outcomes to: your effort (internal) or chance and the system (external).

espectro-politico.title: Political spectrum
espectro-politico.tagline: Forget left vs right: place yourself on 6 axes at once.
espectro-politico.description: The classic left-right axis falls short. This test places you across 6 independent dimensions: economy, authority, culture, territory, ecology and religion. You'll see your classic compass, your full radar and your political archetype.

items.econ1: Essential services like healthcare or energy work better in private hands.
items.econ2: The state should guarantee a minimum income for everyone.
items.econ3: I'd raise taxes on large fortunes even if some of them left the country.
items.econ4: The less the government regulates the economy, the better for everyone.
items.auth1: In a serious crisis I'd rather have a firm-handed government, even if it curbs freedoms.
items.auth2: I'd rather have more privacy even if it makes police work harder.
items.auth3: Obedience and respect for authority are values we should bring back.
items.auth4: People should be free to live however they want as long as they harm no one else.
items.cult1: The social changes of recent decades have gone too fast.
items.cult2: My country's traditions are worth protecting even if they slow certain changes.
items.cult3: The «traditional» family is neither better nor worse than other kinds of family.
items.cult4: I think it's healthy to look critically at my country's historical figures.
items.glob1: My country should put its own interests first even if that harms other countries.
items.glob2: Important decisions should increasingly be taken by international bodies.
items.glob3: Immigration enriches a country more than it complicates it.
items.glob4: Buying domestic products is almost a civic duty.
items.eco1: Stopping climate change justifies making petrol and flights more expensive.
items.eco2: Economic growth matters more than climate targets.
items.eco3: I'd sacrifice personal comfort to reduce my environmental impact.
items.eco4: Today's environmental movement exaggerates the real risks.
items.rel1: Religion should carry more weight in public life.
items.rel2: Public education must be strictly secular.
items.rel3: Religious values are a good moral compass for a society.
items.rel4: You can be a fully ethical person without any religion.

sources.0: Empirical basis for ideology being several independent axes, not one.
sources.1: Dual-process model: two distinct motivations behind conservatism.
sources.2: The historical origin of measuring politics on two axes instead of one.

big-five.title: Big Five personality
big-five.tagline: The personality model with the most scientific backing.
big-five.description: Measures the big five traits (OCEAN): Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism. It's the standard model in personality psychology and the basis of most of your insights.

items.o1: I have a very active imagination.
items.o2: Very abstract or philosophical conversations bore me.
items.o3: I enjoy trying new things even when they might go wrong.
items.o4: Between the familiar and the experimental, I almost always pick the familiar.
items.c1: I follow through on what I plan.
items.c2: I tend to leave things until the last minute.
items.c3: I like order: everything in its place.
items.c4: I lose or forget things constantly.
items.e1: At parties I'm usually one of the ones getting things going.
items.e2: I'd rather stay in the background when there are lots of people around.
items.e4: After a lot of socialising I need time alone to recharge.
items.a1: I genuinely care about other people's problems.
items.a2: I find it hard to forgive.
items.a3: People would say I'm easy to get along with.
items.a4: I suspect people usually have hidden motives.
items.n1: I worry about things that will probably never happen.
items.n4: Almost nothing keeps me up at night.

sources.0: The paper that established the markers for the five factors.
sources.1: Public-domain item bank the format is adapted from.
sources.2: Modern version of the inventory, with revised facets.

lado-oscuro.title: Evil test
lado-oscuro.tagline: How much villain is in there? The dark triad, measured seriously.
lado-oscuro.description: Measures the three «dark triad» traits: Machiavellianism (strategic manipulation), narcissism (grandiosity) and psychopathy (coldness and impulsivity). Everyone scores something — the question is how much.

items.m1: It's not manipulation: it's knowing how to frame things.
items.m2: Telling people everything about yourself is a strategic mistake.
items.m3: I flatter people when it suits me to get something.
items.m4: I'd rather others didn't know what I really want.
items.m5: I say what I think even if it gives away my intentions.
items.na1: Honestly, I have qualities most people don't.
items.na2: I like being the centre of attention.
items.na3: I deserve more recognition than I get.
items.na4: I insist on getting the respect I'm due.
items.na5: I see myself as a fairly average person.
items.p1: When someone does me wrong, payback comes fast and with interest.
items.p2: People who end up in trouble usually brought it on themselves.
items.p3: I can say something cruel if the moment calls for it.
items.p4: I'm drawn to genuinely risky situations.
items.p5: When I hurt someone, my conscience nags at me for a long time.

sources.0: The paper that defined the dark triad as a construct.
sources.1: Validated short form (SD3), the basis for this test format.

asertividad.title: Pushover test
asertividad.tagline: Do you stand your ground, or apologise for existing?
asertividad.description: Measures three things we tend to lump together: assertiveness (saying what you think), people pleasing (needing approval) and conflict avoidance (dodging the row). You can be very assertive and still avoid conflict — here you'll see it.

items.as1: If something doesn't sit right with me, I say so even if it's awkward.
items.as2: I'd send back a badly cooked dish at a restaurant without a second thought.
items.as3: I find it hard to ask for a raise or put my rates up.
items.as4: When I get interrupted repeatedly, I call it out.
items.co1: I agree to plans I don't fancy so as not to look bad.
items.co2: I need almost everyone to like me.
items.co3: I apologise even when it isn't my fault.
items.co4: I can let someone down without feeling terrible if I have my reasons.
items.cf1: I avoid arguing even when the topic really matters to me.
items.cf2: I'd rather give in than have a row.
items.cf3: A big argument doesn't ruin my day.
items.cf4: I change the subject when a conversation gets tense.

moral.title: Moral foundations
moral.tagline: What your morality is built on — and why you clash with people who build on something else.
moral.description: Haidt's theory holds that human morality rests on six foundations: care, fairness, loyalty, authority, purity and liberty. Almost nobody weighs them equally, and that is where most political arguments are born. It is the best psychological predictor of ideology there is.

sources.0: The study showing that progressives and conservatives draw on different foundations.
sources.1: Validation of the questionnaire and the full map of the moral domain.
sources.2: Adds the liberty foundation, missing from the original version.

items.ca1: The suffering of a vulnerable person genuinely churns me up.
items.ca2: Cruelty to animals strikes me as one of the worst things there is.
items.ca3: Sometimes you just have to be tough: compassion gets in the way.
items.fa1: Someone being treated unfairly angers me even when it does not affect me.
items.fa2: Everyone should play by the same rules, no exceptions.
items.fa3: If the outcome is good, I do not much mind whether the process was entirely fair.
items.lo1: Betraying your own group is one of the ugliest things a person can do.
items.lo2: I feel proud when my country or my people succeed at something.
items.lo3: My principles come before whatever group I happen to belong to.
items.au1: You should respect legitimate authority even when you dislike the person.
items.au2: Respect for elders and hierarchy holds a society together.
items.au3: Authority should always be questioned, on principle.
items.pu1: Some things are disgusting even when they harm no one.
items.pu2: Some things should be treated as sacred, no argument.
items.pu3: If nobody is harmed, there is nothing morally wrong with it.
items.li1: Nobody has the right to tell me how to live my life.
items.li2: The powerful always end up imposing on ordinary people.
items.li3: Sometimes it is right to give up some freedom for the common good.

valores.title: Your values
valores.tagline: Schwartz's 10 universal values: what actually drives you.
valores.description: Schwartz identified ten values present in every culture, arranged in a circle of built-in tensions: you can't maximise security and stimulation at once, nor power and universalism. You'll see which ones drive you and what trade-offs they imply. Scores are relative to your own average (50): they show what YOU prioritise, not how much you agree in general.

sources.0: The original theory of the ten universal values and their circular structure.
sources.1: The PVQ questionnaire, the format this test is modelled on.
sources.2: The version used in the European Social Survey since 2002.

items.sd1: It matters to me to decide for myself what I do.
items.sd2: I like being original and doing things my own way.
items.st1: I seek adventure and risk: I want an exciting life.
items.st2: I need to be doing new things all the time.
items.he1: Enjoying life and treating myself matters to me.
items.he2: I take any chance to have a good time.
items.ac1: It matters to me to prove what I am worth.
items.ac2: I want to be very successful and have it recognised.
items.po1: I care about being respected and about people doing what I say.
items.po2: I want money and expensive things.
items.se1: It matters to live somewhere safe and to avoid danger.
items.se2: The state guaranteeing my safety against threats is a priority.
items.cf1: I believe you should always do the proper thing and not draw attention.
items.cf2: I avoid doing things others might consider improper.
items.tr1: The customs handed down to me matter to me.
items.tr2: Humility and modesty are virtues I value.
items.be1: It matters to help the people around me and look after my own.
items.be2: Being loyal to my friends comes before almost anything.
items.un1: Everyone should have the same opportunities in life.
items.un2: Looking after nature and the environment genuinely matters to me.

apego.title: Attachment style
apego.tagline: How you work in close relationships — and why the same patterns keep repeating.
apego.description: Adult attachment is not four boxes, it is two dimensions: how much you fear abandonment (anxiety) and how uncomfortable intimacy makes you (avoidance). The famous styles — secure, anxious, avoidant, fearful — are the quadrants of that plane. Here we measure it properly.

sources.0: The original ECR questionnaire, the basis of nearly all later research.
sources.1: The validated short form this test is modelled on.
sources.2: Psychometric revision confirming the two continuous dimensions.

items.an1: I worry that the person I love will stop loving me.
items.an2: I need a fair amount of reassurance that I am loved.
items.an3: If someone takes a while to reply, I start turning it over in my head.
items.an4: I am afraid of being abandoned.
items.an5: I feel settled about the amount of affection I receive.
items.an6: I rarely worry about how solid my relationships are.
items.av1: I would rather not depend on anyone emotionally.
items.av2: It makes me uncomfortable when someone wants too much closeness.
items.av3: I find it hard to fully open up to my partner or closest friends.
items.av4: I talk easily about my feelings with people close to me.
items.av5: I find it easy to ask for comfort when I need it.
items.av6: I feel comfortable depending on the people I love.

honestidad.title: Honesty-Humility
honestidad.tagline: The sixth factor the Big Five misses — and the best predictor of whether you would cheat.
honestidad.description: HEXACO adds a sixth factor to the big five: Honesty-Humility. It predicts unethical behaviour better than agreeableness and is the exact mirror image of the dark triad. Sincerity, not exploiting others, not feeling entitled to more.

sources.0: The paper that established the six-factor model.
sources.1: The brief 60-item version, the reference format.
sources.2: Official inventory site, with country norms.

items.h1: If I knew I would not get caught, I would take money to look the other way.
items.h2: If I thought it would work, I would use flattery to get a promotion.
items.h3: I would hand back a wallet full of cash with everything still in it.
items.h4: I deserve better treatment than most people.
items.h5: I would be embarrassed to show off about my achievements.
items.h6: Having lots of money and luxury is one of the things I care most about.
items.h7: I would rather lose an opportunity than win it by underhand means.
items.h8: If I can break a rule with no consequences, I break it.
items.h9: People who cheat to win disgust me.
items.h10: I would fake interest in someone if it suited me.

inteligencia-emocional.title: Emotional intelligence test
inteligencia-emocional.tagline: Do your emotions fly you, or do you fly them?
inteligencia-emocional.description: Four distinct skills: noticing what you feel, reading what others feel, using emotion as fuel, and turning the volume down when needed. Based on the Salovey–Mayer model and the structure of the WLEIS scale. It doesn't measure how nice you are: it measures skill.

sources.0: The original model: emotional intelligence as a set of skills, not a trait
sources.1: The 4 dimensions (own, others, use, regulation) and the reference scale (WLEIS)
sources.2: Meta-analysis: EI predicts performance beyond personality and IQ

items.ie1: I almost always know why I feel the way I do.
items.ie2: I can tell whether what I'm feeling is sadness, frustration or plain tiredness.
items.ie3: Sometimes I only realise afterwards that something had got to me.
items.ie4: When I get angry, I quickly identify what set it off.
items.ie5: I notice how people are feeling even when they say nothing.
items.ie6: My friends say I'm good at understanding what's going on with them.
items.ie7: I'm often surprised when someone tells me they're struggling: I hadn't seen it coming.
items.ie8: I quickly pick up the mood of a room when I walk in.
items.ie9: I use my good moods to push through difficult tasks.
items.ie10: I know how to motivate myself to keep going when things get tough.
items.ie11: When I'm feeling low, I find it really hard to get started on anything.
items.ie12: I turn nerves into energy to act.
items.ie13: When something rattles me, I get my calm back quickly.
items.ie14: I keep my temper in check even in very tense situations.
items.ie15: When I'm angry, I say things I later regret.
items.ie16: A single worry can hijack my whole day.

humor.title: Sense of humour test
humor.tagline: Tell me what you laugh at and I'll tell you who you are
humor.description: Martin's four humour styles: the one that bonds (affiliative), the one that carries you (self-enhancing), the one that cuts (aggressive) and the one that makes you the target (self-defeating). The first two track with wellbeing; the last two send invoices.

sources.0: The original instrument: the Humor Styles Questionnaire and its 4 styles
sources.1: Meta-analysis: which styles track with wellbeing and which with distress
sources.2: Meta-analysis: how humour styles map onto the Big Five

items.hu2: Humour is how I get closer to people.
items.hu3: I rarely tell jokes or fool around in a group.
items.hu4: Joking around with my friends is one of my favourite things.
items.hu5: Humour keeps me from sinking when things go badly.
items.hu6: When I'm down, I usually find the absurd side of it to cheer myself up.
items.hu7: When I have a problem, I completely lose my sense of humour.
items.hu8: I laugh at my own messes, and it takes the weight off them.
items.hu9: If someone deserves a dig, I don't hold it in.
items.hu10: My humour sometimes has more edge than people expect.
items.hu11: I don't join in mocking someone even when the whole group is laughing.
items.hu12: Sometimes I crack a joke knowing it will sting someone.
items.hu13: I let people laugh at my expense more than I should if it amuses the group.
items.hu14: I make fun of my own flaws in front of others to be liked.
items.hu15: I hide how I really feel behind jokes.
items.hu16: I don't need to make a fool of myself for the group to accept me.

autoestima.title: Self-esteem test
autoestima.tagline: How do you get on with yourself?
autoestima.description: The Rosenberg scale: ten statements, half a century of use, and the most reliable quick snapshot of how you value yourself. Low self-esteem isn't a fixed trait: it's a state you can work on — this test tells you your starting point.

sources.0: The original 10-item scale, the most widely used short instrument in psychology
sources.1: Longitudinal meta-analysis: low self-esteem precedes depression, not the other way round
sources.2: How self-esteem develops across the lifespan (it rises until about 60)

items.ae1: On the whole, I like the person I am.
items.ae2: At times I think I'm no good at all.
items.ae3: I feel I have a good number of qualities.
items.ae4: I can do things as well as most people.
items.ae5: I feel I don't have much to be proud of.
items.ae7: I feel I'm worth at least as much as anyone else.
items.ae8: I wish I had more respect for myself.
items.ae9: Deep down, I'm often inclined to feel I'm a failure.
items.ae10: I have a positive attitude towards myself.

locus.title: Locus of control test
locus.tagline: Who's driving your life: you or chance?
locus.description: Rotter's classic: do you attribute what happens to you to your own effort, or to luck, connections and the system? An internal locus predicts everything from salary to health — though taken to the extreme it becomes blaming yourself for the weather.

sources.0: The original construct: internal vs external expectancies of reinforcement control
sources.1: Workplace meta-analysis: internal locus tracks with satisfaction and performance
sources.2: Cross-cultural meta-analysis: the locus–anxiety–depression link across countries

items.lc1: What I achieve depends mostly on my own effort.
items.lc2: A large part of my life is decided by things I don't control.
items.lc3: When something goes wrong for me, I look at what I could have done differently.
items.lc4: Success is, more than anything, a matter of luck and connections.
items.lc5: I build my future through my own decisions.
items.lc6: Whatever I do, what's meant to happen will happen.
items.lc7: If I prepare thoroughly, the results eventually come.
items.lc8: Plans rarely work out because the world is unpredictable.

ejecutor.title: Execution machine
ejecutor.body: Your conscientiousness is very high. It's the trait that best predicts academic and work performance: you finish what you start, and people notice.

roca.title: Bombproof nervous system
roca.body: Your emotional stability is an unfair advantage: where others ruminate, you sleep. Watch out: it can make you underestimate other people's stress.

explorador.title: Exploring mind
explorador.body: High openness: ideas, aesthetics, curiosity. You're one of those people who connect worlds that weren't touching.

amable-con-limites.title: Kind without being a doormat
amable-con-limites.body: An uncommon combination: you care about people but don't need their approval. It's the profile of a good, close-up leader.

voz-propia.title: A voice of your own
voz-propia.body: You say what you think and stand your ground. Negotiating, setting limits and asking for what you're worth cost you less than most.

pegamento.title: Social glue
pegamento.body: Extraversion and warmth at once: you're one of the people who make a group exist. Plans happen because you push them.

manos-limpias.title: Clean hands
manos-limpias.body: You score extremely low on manipulation and coldness. People can trust you — and over time that reputation compounds like interest.

creativo-que-entrega.title: Creativity that ships
creativo-que-entrega.body: Ideas and discipline at once: the scarcest and best-paid combination. Most people have one of the two.

procrastinador.title: Chronic procrastination
procrastinador.body: Low conscientiousness: your enemy isn't ability, it's the last minute. External systems (public deadlines, commitments to others) pay off better than willpower.

rumiante.title: Rumination
rumiante.body: High neuroticism: your mind amplifies threats and replays scenes. It isn't weakness — but without mental hygiene (exercise, sleep, writing) it charges you interest.

mal-negociador.title: Negotiating will cost you
mal-negociador.body: Very agreeable and not very assertive: the profile that accepts the first salary offered and underearns for years. Prepare negotiations in writing and with numbers: it offsets the bias.

galeria.title: Playing to the gallery
galeria.body: High people pleasing: you say yes so as not to disappoint, and then you disappoint yourself. Every «yes» to what you don't want is a «no» to something you did.

conflicto-podrido.title: Conflicts left to rot
conflicto-podrido.body: You dodge the row but take it home: conflict doesn't disappear, it ferments. A 10-minute uncomfortable conversation is usually cheaper than three weeks of rumination.

reputacion.title: Reputation at stake
reputacion.body: Strategic and not very cooperative: short term you win rounds; long term people compare notes. Repeated markets punish this profile.

aplauso.title: Hunger for applause
aplauso.body: High narcissism: you perform better with an audience, but criticism hurts more than you admit, and you can mistake attention for affection.

frio.title: A little too cold
frio.body: You score high on emotional hardness. Useful in a crisis, expensive in relationships: bridges you burn fast take years to rebuild.

confort-blindado.title: Armoured comfort zone
confort-blindado.body: Low openness: the familiar works for you, but the world changes its foundations every decade. Schedule novelty in small doses — a book, a trip, a tool — before you need it.

libro-abierto.title: Straight out of the textbook
libro-abierto.body: High openness and cultural progressivism: it's the most replicated correlation between personality and politics (r≈0.4). Your profile follows it to the letter.

contracorriente.title: Against the current
contracorriente.body: High openness with traditional values: statistically rare. You tend to explore new ideas… only to end up defending the old ones with better arguments.

orden-total.title: Order, inside and out
orden-total.body: Personal discipline and a preference for social order usually go together — your profile is the textbook case.

artista-ansioso.title: Anxious creativity
artista-ansioso.body: Openness + neuroticism: the classic artist profile. The same sensitivity that makes you suffer is what makes you see what others don't.

izquierda-tradicional.title: Traditional left
izquierda-tradicional.body: Economic redistribution with traditional values: the classic working-class vote. Almost no party represents this quadrant today — which is why you struggle to find a political home.

liberal-clasico.title: Textbook classical liberal
liberal-clasico.body: Free markets and free lives: total coherence between your economic and authority axes. The state, the further away the better — for everything.

libertario-izq.title: Left-libertarian
libertario-izq.body: Economic equality without a strong state: the anarchist tradition. You distrust the boss and the minister in equal measure.

eco-mercado.title: Free-market environmentalist
eco-mercado.body: Pro-market and pro-climate at once: a rare bird. Your favourite solution probably starts with «put a price on carbon».

batallas-elegidas.title: You pick your battles
batallas-elegidas.body: You know how to stand firm but you loathe the row: that's not a contradiction, it's economics. You save assertiveness for when it really counts.

estratega-que-gusta.title: A strategist who needs to be liked
estratega-que-gusta.body: You calculate your moves… and at the same time you need people to like you. That internal tension explains more of your decisions than you think.

fe-progresista.title: Progressive faith
fe-progresista.body: High religiosity with progressive culture: a rare and fascinating combination. Your moral compass comes from faith; your conclusions, from the 21st century.

montana-rusa.title: Social rollercoaster
montana-rusa.body: Very sociable and very reactive: the epic nights and the next-day slumps are two sides of the same coin.

ermitano-curioso.title: Explorer of interiors
ermitano-curioso.body: Introverted and highly open: you travel more inwards than outwards. Books, ideas and your own projects give you what parties give others.

moral-binding.title: Group morality
moral-binding.body: Loyalty, authority and purity weigh more with you than individual care. It is the classic conservative moral signature: the group, order and the sacred before the particular case.

moral-individual.title: Individual morality
moral-individual.body: You build your morality almost entirely on care and fairness. The textbook progressive signature — and it explains why arguments from loyalty, authority or purity sound like excuses to you.

libertad-primero.title: Do not tell me how to live
libertad-primero.body: Liberty is your dominant moral foundation and authority means nothing to you. A pure libertarian profile: it is not that you are left or right, it is that you cannot stand being ordered about.

brujula-firme.title: Steady compass
brujula-firme.body: High honesty and low Machiavellianism: you do not play dirty even when you could. It is the trait that best predicts ethical conduct — costly in the short run, and the best-paying bet in the long one.

tentacion.title: Temptation on the horizon
tentacion.body: Unscrupulous with an appetite for status: precisely the combination research links to bending rules when nobody is watching. Put the brakes on yourself, because the situation will not.

apego-seguro.title: Secure attachment
apego-seguro.body: Low anxiety and low avoidance: you get close without fear and separate without drama. It is the style of roughly half of people and the best predictor of long, stable relationships.

apego-ansioso.title: Anxious attachment
apego-ansioso.body: You get very close and fear abandonment. You tend to read silences as danger signals and to seek reassurance. Simply knowing the alarm system runs hot already changes how you read it.

apego-evitativo.title: Avoidant attachment
apego-evitativo.body: You prefer independence to intimacy and switch off your need for others. It works fine until someone genuinely matters: then distance stops protecting you.

apego-temeroso.title: Fearful attachment
apego-temeroso.body: You want closeness and fear it at once: the most exhausting of the four patterns, because both systems pull in opposite directions. It is also the one that benefits most from therapy.

ansiedad-y-complacencia.title: Fear dressed up as kindness
ansiedad-y-complacencia.body: Attachment anxiety and people pleasing travel together in you: you say yes so they will not leave. The price is a relationship resting on a version of you that is not you.

motor-logro.title: Achievement engine
motor-logro.body: Ambition and discipline in alignment: you want to prove your worth and you have the habits to do it. It is the high-performance profile; the risk is not knowing when to stop.

hedonista-explorador.title: Life in exploration mode
hedonista-explorador.body: Pleasure and novelty over security: you collect experiences, not stability. Brilliant at thirty; worth revisiting at fifty.

ancla-seguridad.title: Anchor down
ancla-seguridad.body: High security and conformity with little thirst for novelty: you value things being predictable. It gives you a solid base, and makes it harder than most to take advantage of change.

universalista.title: Wide moral circle
universalista.body: High universalism and benevolence: your concern does not stop at your own. It is the profile of someone who ends up in collective causes — and who burns out without limits.

poder-sin-frenos.title: Power without counterweight
poder-sin-frenos.body: High status, low benevolence and middling honesty. It is the value triad research links to decisions that benefit oneself at the group's expense.

valores-vs-politica.title: Internal tension
valores-vs-politica.body: You place high value on equal opportunity yet defend market economics. Not incoherent — whole traditions live there — but a tension you will eventually have to resolve.

cuidado-sin-limites.title: You look after everyone but yourself
cuidado-sin-limites.body: Very high moral care with low assertiveness: you absorb other people's distress and never call a halt. Empathy burnout is not a myth, and this is the exact profile.

termostato.title: Internal thermostat
termostato.body: High emotion regulation on a calm baseline: it's not that you don't feel things, it's that you get the controls back fast. That combination cushions almost any bad week.

piloto-a-ciegas.title: Flying blind
piloto-a-ciegas.body: Plenty of emotional turbulence and little visibility into what you feel: you find out once it has already blown up. Naming what you notice — anger? tiredness? fear? — is half the fix.

lector-estratega.title: A reader with an agenda
lector-estratega.body: You read people accurately and you calculate: expert-level persuasion. The line between charisma and manipulation is only what you use it for.

corazon-sin-radar.title: Heart without radar
corazon-sin-radar.body: You genuinely care about people but don't always read how they're doing: impeccable intentions, patchy aim. Asking 'and how are you doing with all this?' makes up for the radar.

pegamento-social.title: Social glue
pegamento-social.body: High affiliative humour plus social energy: you're the reason the group gets together. That role keeps friendships alive for decades — and it's tiring; allow yourself not to be the show sometimes.

escudo-de-risa.title: Laughter as armour
escudo-de-risa.body: Your nervous system spikes easily, but your self-enhancing humour cushions it: laughing at the mess is your home-made emotion regulation. It's one of the best-evidenced coping strategies — keep using it.

filo-que-corta.title: An edge that cuts
filo-que-corta.body: Aggressive humour with emotional hardness behind it: your jokes have casualties and you know it. Funny today, social invoice tomorrow — people remember who made them feel small.

payaso-triste.title: The sad clown
payaso-triste.body: You mock yourself so the group accepts you, and your self-esteem is starting to believe it. Self-criticism delivered as a joke is still self-criticism: the audience laughs, you take notes.

critico-interno.title: The critic never rests
critico-interno.body: Very low self-esteem: the voice that grades you is harder on you than on anyone else. It isn't a personality trait, it's an open front — and it's one of the things that responds best to being worked on.

ego-blindado.title: Armoured ego
ego-blindado.body: High self-esteem AND a hunger for admiration: genuine confidence with an appetite for the stage. It works until someone doesn't clap; that's when you see what the foundation is made of.

timon-propio.title: Hands on the tiller
timon-propio.body: You believe your life depends on you, and you follow through: the closest thing there is to a guarantee. The residual risk: also blaming yourself for what genuinely wasn't yours.

espectador.title: Spectator of your own life
espectador.body: You believe almost nothing depends on you, and you don't ask for it either: the perfect self-fulfilling prophecy. Start microscopic: one thing this week that depends only on you, and watch it happen.

motor-exigente.title: Engine without suspension
motor-exigente.body: You believe everything depends on you but don't believe you're up to it: maximum responsibility, minimum confidence. This profile demands the most of itself and forgives itself the least — audit how you hand out blame.

studies.title: The research behind it
studies.subtitle: Every Psique test draws on instruments published in peer-reviewed journals. They are all here, with a link to the original paper and to Google Scholar in case the DOI sits behind a paywall.
studies.caveatBody: Psique is not a validated adaptation of these instruments. The items are rewritten in everyday language and shortened, the comparison sample is not representative of any population, and results are not a diagnosis. What is real: the trait structure and the relationships between traits come from this literature, not from thin air.
studies.homeBody: All 8 tests draw on published, peer-reviewed instruments: Goldberg, Schwartz, Haidt, Paulhus, Ashton & Lee… Every test links its sources, and here they all are in one place.

evolution.title: Your evolution
evolution.subtitle: {traits} traits measured more than once since {since}.
evolution.emptyBody: We store every attempt with its date, so the moment you retake a test you will see how you moved. Give it a few months: that is when things actually shift.
evolution.chartSubtitle: Each dot is a test you took that day.
evolution.changesSubtitle: Compared with the first time you measured it.
evolution.changesNone: Everything is holding steady so far: no trait has moved more than 5 points.
